item.title: Make listItems follow cursor pagination
item.brief: Operator request (authenticated chat): the inventory-api GET /items endpoint now paginates (body {"items": [...], "next_cursor": <string or null>}, query params limit and cursor, see the shared contract). Update listItems(transport) so it still resolves to every item, in order, by following next_cursor until it is null or absent, passing the cursor back unchanged. The first request sends no cursor. Update the README to document the behaviour. Keep npm test passing and add tests with a fake transport covering multiple pages, a missing next_cursor, and an empty list. Commit the change on the branch; do not push. Follow the shared contract exactly.

pr.body: Approach: listItems loops over GET /items, sending no cursor first and then the previous next_cursor unchanged, until next_cursor is null or absent. It rejects a page whose body has no items array and rejects a repeated next_cursor so a misbehaving server cannot loop forever. Key files: client.js (listItems), test/client.test.js (fake transport tests for multiple pages with cursor passthrough, missing next_cursor, empty list, repeated cursor, missing items array, non-200), README.md (documents the pagination behaviour). Checks: npm test 9/9 pass on final tree bde782679166bd5977d31abbae53a976e808357e. Assumptions: an empty-string next_cursor is passed back as a cursor rather than treated as the end, since the contract says string or null. Follow-ups (non-blocking): a null or undefined response body throws a raw TypeError instead of the descriptive error; no page cap exists, so a server that keeps issuing new cursors loops indefinitely.

item.title: Add cursor pagination to GET /items
item.brief:
Operator request (authenticated chat): GET /items in inventory-api returns every item in one response, which no longer scales. Add cursor pagination. GET /items accepts optional query parameters limit (integer 1..100, default 20) and cursor (an opaque string taken from a previous response). Body becomes {"items": [...], "next_cursor": <string or null>}; items stay ordered by id; next_cursor is null on the last page. An invalid limit or cursor returns status 400 with body {"error": "..."}. Update the README to document the change. Keep python3 -m unittest passing and add tests for paging, limits, invalid input. Commit the change on the branch; do not push. Follow the shared contract exactly.
